attempted_claim: Let M=CP^2 with ordered configurations F_k(M) and unordered B_k(M)=F_k(M)/S_k, and let V^{(1)}_k be the reduced standard S_k-representation Q^k modulo the diagonal, viewed as a degree-1 twisted coefficient system on B_k(M) via the regular cover F_k(M)->B_k(M). Using the Fadell-Neuwirth fibration F_k(M)->F_{k-1}(M) with fiber M minus k-1 points and its Serre spectral sequence with local coefficients, prove or disprove that the puncture-stabilization maps induce isomorphisms H_i(B_k(CP^2);V^{(1)}_k)->H_i(B_{k+1}(CP^2);V^{(1)}_{k+1}) for all i>=0 whenever k>=2i+4, and that the slope 2 is best possible ( witnessed by an explicit infinite family of pairs (k,i) with k=2i+3 and non-isomorphic twisted homology). A complete answer is a proof of the full range plus slope-sharpness witnesses, or one explicit verified pair (k,i) with k>=2i+4 where the twisted stabilization map fails to be an isomorphism.
claim_type: twisted stability isomorphism with slope sharpness
decisive_failure: The exact Totaro verification machine is sound only through degree 7 (R2=0 checks, drop justification, and block-disjointness audit all pass there); at degree 8 the x-shifted Arnold relations project to zero under invariant orbit sums, so no certified statement is made about t_8 or higher degrees, the sharpness family at k=2i+3, or the full k>=2i+4 range, which remain open.
